21.name: File Transfer (FTP)
21.description: Used for uploading or downloading files (insecure).

22.name: Remote Access (SSH)
22.description: The standard way for technicians to remotely manage computers via command line (high security).

23.name: Remote Terminal (Telnet)
23.description: An older, unencrypted way of remote control (insecure).

25.name: Email Sending (SMTP)
25.description: Channel for sending emails to servers. Usually unencrypted.

53.name: URL Translation (DNS)
53.description: Translates website names (like google.com) to IP addresses. Essential for internet connectivity.

67.name: Automatic Network Setup (DHCP Server)
67.description: Used to automatically assign IP addresses to devices on a network.

68.name: Automatic Network Setup (DHCP Client)
68.description: The channel used to request an IP address from a network.

69.name: Simple File Transfer (TFTP)
69.description: A basic file transfer protocol, often used for backing up network device configurations. Unencrypted.

80.name: Web Browsing (HTTP)
80.description: General web browsing. Data is unencrypted; not suitable for sensitive information.

110.name: Email Retrieval (POP3)
110.description: An older protocol for downloading emails (insecure).

111.name: Resource Sharing (RPCbind)
111.description: A basic service that helps computers find shared resources.

123.name: Time Sync (NTP)
123.description: Automatically synchronizes the time between computers and servers.

135.name: Windows Internal Communication (RPC)
135.description: An internal channel used for Windows services to talk to each other.

137.name: Network Neighborhood (NetBIOS)
137.description: Used to find other computers or resources on a local network.

138.name: Network Broadcast (NetBIOS)
138.description: Used to send broadcast messages to let other computers know you are present.

139.name: File Sharing (NetBIOS)
139.description: An older protocol for sharing files or printers on a local network.

143.name: Email Access (IMAP)
143.description: A modern protocol for accessing emails, more advanced than POP3.

161.name: Network Monitoring (SNMP)
161.description: Used for monitoring the status of network devices like routers or switches.

162.name: Alert Notification (SNMP Trap)
162.description: A channel for network devices to send alerts when anomalies occur.

443.name: Secure Web Browsing (HTTPS)
443.description: Encrypted web browsing to protect your data transfer (high security).

445.name: Windows File Sharing (SMB)
445.description: The core protocol for sharing folders and printers in modern Windows.

500.name: VPN Security Authentication
500.description: Exchanges encryption keys when establishing a VPN connection.

514.name: System Logs (Syslog)
514.description: Sends operation logs from devices to a central server for storage.

520.name: Routing Information (RIP)
520.description: Used by routers to exchange network path information.

631.name: Network Printing (IPP)
631.description: Manages and sends print jobs to network printers.

993.name: Secure Email Access (IMAPS)
993.description: IMAP email retrieval using SSL encryption (high security).

995.name: Secure Email Retrieval (POP3S)
995.description: POP3 email retrieval using SSL encryption (high security).

1434.name: Database Discovery (SQL Server)
1434.description: Used to locate Microsoft SQL servers on the local network.

1723.name: Virtual Private Network (VPN)
1723.description: A channel for establishing VPN connections, often used to connect to corporate networks.

1900.name: Device Discovery (UPnP)
1900.description: Allows network devices (like smart home gadgets) to identify each other automatically.

3306.name: Database Service (MySQL)
3306.description: MySQL database communication port, used by websites for data storage.

3389.name: Remote Desktop (RDP)
3389.description: Windows remote desktop control, allows direct operation of another screen.

4500.name: VPN Data Channel
4500.description: Used for transferring encrypted data in a VPN connection.

5900.name: Desktop Sharing (VNC)
5900.description: A cross-platform desktop sharing system for remote screen control.

8080.name: Web Proxy/Testing
8080.description: Often used as a backup web port or a proxy server.

49152.name: Dynamic Service Port
49152.description: A temporary channel randomly assigned by the system to applications.
